summary: Margaret Dornish is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).
Margaret Gouin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bristol, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams.

Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at DePauw, Barnard, and Columbia under Franz Boas. She held long-term posts at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969) and Columbia University (1954–1978), and also served at Fordham University (1968–1970).

Margaret R. Miles (born 1937) is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. After earning degrees from SFSU and the Graduate Theological Union, she taught at Harvard (1978–1996) and served as dean of the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer works in religious studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and completed postdoctoral work mentored by Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya (1933–2021) specialized in Buddhist, Iranian/Central Asian, and Indological studies. She studied at St. Petersburg University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, serving at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2010) and as manuscripts curator (1982–2005).
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She pursued her studies under Karin Preisendanz and MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Maria Heim is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard under Charles Hallisey. She has served as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Maria Krzysztof Byrski (born 1937) is an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1955–1960). He later served there as Head of the Indology Department (~1990–1993) and held a post at Civitas University.

Marian Ury (1932–1995) was a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, and served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis from 1969 to 1995.

Marianne Pieper (born 1949) studied at Hamburger Hochschule für Wirtschaft und Politik and completed her Habilitation at Magdeburg (1996). She held temporary chairs at Hamburg and Kassel, and was Professor of Sociology at the University of Hamburg (1996–2015).

Marianne Winder (1918–2001) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies after studying at London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. She held posts at Nottingham, the IGRS, and the Wellcome Institute, where she was curator and consultant.
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania, where she was a student of Sengaku Mayeda.

Marielle Harrison specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. A doctoral student at the University of Chicago, she is attested in 2026 as an HCBSS Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer at Stanford University.
Marina Illich is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her PhD at Columbia University in 2006 under Robert A. F. Thurman.

Mario D'Amato is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He held posts at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and Rollins College.

Mario Poceski specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD in 2000 from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and held an assistant professorship at the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).
Mario Praz (1896–1982) studied at the universities of Bologna and Florence. He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Marion Meyer (born 1954) is a scholar in history and archaeology. She held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), University of Florida (1996), University of Bonn (~1997–2003), and University of Vienna (~2003).
